title: Lot Size Calculator: Acres and Square Feet
description: Calculate a rectangular lot's size from its dimensions with the Lot Size Calculator — square feet, acres and hectares from length and width. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 100 × 150 ft lot is 15,000 square feet — 0.344 acres — while doubling both sides to 200 × 300 ft quadruples it to 1.377 acres, not doubles.
quick_answer: The Lot Size Calculator multiplies a rectangular lot's length and width into its area, reported in square feet, acres, hectares and square metres. Enter the two dimensions and read the size in every unit a listing or deed might use — the arithmetic behind 'quarter-acre lot'.

body.t: ‘Quarter-acre lot’ with 60 × 150 ft dimensions? That is 9,000 sq ft — 0.207 acre, and the claim is generous. The calculator is the lie detector; the missing-side solvers (
Lot Depth From Area and Width
) help when a dimension is coy.
A European 800 m² plot and an American 8,600 sq ft lot are near-twins (800 m² ≈ 8,611 sq ft). One calculator, both dialects, no conversion errors.
Per-acre pricing, seed, mulch, mowing and fencing all begin with area. This is the number they consume — get it here once, correctly.
A 200 × 300 ft homesite at 1.377 acres plans very differently from its 0.344-acre suburban cousin — buildings, septic, orchard and ego all scale with the area.

One acre as a square has sides of 208.7 ft — a useful mental picture: an American football field is 1.32 acres including end zones, and a square acre is a bit under three-quarters of the field's footprint.
100 × 150 ft = 0.344 acre; 200 × 300 ft = 1.377 acres. Area grows with the square of dimension — the most underestimated multiplication in property browsing.

faq: What if my lot is a triangle or trapezoid?
Triangles take base × height ÷ 2, trapezoids average the parallel sides — but the honest general tool is drawing the parcel in the Map Area Calculator, which prices any shape geodesically.
Are easements and road frontage included?
Deed area usually includes land under easements and sometimes to the road's centreline. The calculator computes the dimensions you give it; what the law counts is a title question.
Enter metres and read every unit — 20 × 40 m is 800 m², 0.198 acre. No pre-conversion needed.
Why doesn't my survey match the listing?
Listings round, borrow from tax records, or err. The survey is the legal instrument; the calculator's role is exposing the gap in thirty seconds.
Slope, wetlands, floodplain and setbacks shrink usable land below deed area. This page gives the deed number; the buildable number needs the local rules applied to it.
Zoning sets minimum lot sizes and densities — divide your area by the zone's minimum and you have the theoretical count, before roads and reality take their share.
Exact for the inputs. Tape-measure inputs give tape-measure truth: a 1% error in each side is a 2% error in area, which on an acre is 871 sq ft of fiction.
